topics.label: Welcome and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The opening introduces the lecturer, learning objectives, and main themes regarding what causes cancer.

topics.label: Intrinsic mutations, environmental risk factors, and epidemiological patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the broad origins of cancer by evaluating how endogenous mutational processes, inherited predisposition, and environmental exposures interact across populations.

topics.label: Pathogens and viral mechanisms of oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive malignant transformation, focusing on viral oncogenesis and the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how various environmental agents, such as dietary toxins, UV radiation, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, herbicides, and aromatic amines, cause direct and indirect DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, multi-stage carcinogenesis, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, contrasting tumor initiators with promoters and assessing how chronic inflammation and life-stage developmental windows influence susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for identifying, profiling, and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the experimental and observational methodologies used to detect carcinogenicity, including mutational signatures, biobanks, rodent assays, and in vitro tests.
